notes: Site: beruru.com (Shopify, myshopify domain beruru-shop). Access: robots.txt fetched cleanly at https://beruru.com/robots.txt (no Claude-specific disallow; general 'Allow: /' for crawlers), so tier-1 direct HTTP fetch was used throughout - no block encountered this session. Discovery: fetched sitemap.xml -> sitemap_collections_1.xml (98 collection handles) and found 4 best-selling-* handles: best-sellers, best-selling-planters, best-selling-furnitures, best-selling-decor. None of these 4 appear in the homepage's rendered main-nav collection links (checked via raw HTML href scan), so they are reachable via sitemap/direct-URL only, not top nav - still valid per brief (sitemap is an explicit discovery channel). Each was opened and confirmed as a real PLP: og:title/h1 match the handle's expected name and each page shows a live 'N products' count matching an exhaustive /collections/<handle>/products.json?limit=250 enumeration (all 4 totals are well under the 250-per-page cap, so each count is complete/exact, not paginated). Sub-structure decision: breadcrumbs on the 3 category-specific pages are flat (Home > <name>, no explicit 'Best Sellers' parent link in the UI), but product-set analysis proves genuine nesting: all 18 Best Selling Planters, all 20 Best Selling Furnitures, and all 12 Best Selling Decor product handles are a strict subset of the 109 handles on /collections/best-sellers (50 of 109 accounted for by the three category cuts, the remaining 59 are other categories such as lighting/tableware bestsellers not given their own dedicated URL). This is treated as genuine site-defined sub-structure (parent 'Best Sellers' + 3 category-scoped children), not an alias/duplicate, since the children are proper subsets with distinct, non-overlapping URLs and distinct on-page identities. No other Bestsellers-type term (Top Sellers/Most Popular/Trending/Customer Favorites) found in sitemap, nav, or Shopify's own predictive-search collection results (checked via /search/suggest.json - see cl257.json/na257.json notes for that same check). Excluded as unrelated to this concept: 'Fresh Picks' (curated 'stylish/luxury' merchandising bucket per its own meta description, not a bestseller signal) and 'High Value Products' (a price-tier bucket).
